rationale: This is clearly property damage to the policyholder's own insured structure. The fire originated from the claimant's stove (an appliance within their home), causing direct physical damage to kitchen cabinets and smoke damage to ceilings and walls. This is a straightforward property damage claim covered under homeowners insurance.
claim_summary: Homeowners policy POL-1001 (Alex Doe). Fire claim originating from grease flare-up on kitchen stove yesterday evening. Damage includes charred kitchen cabinets above stove and smoke damage on ceiling and walls. Fire was extinguished by claimant using fire extinguisher. No injuries. Damage contained to kitchen area. Deductible: $500; Coverage limit: $250,000. Severity: Medium. Estimated loss range: $5,000–$25,000. Requires contractor assessment and photographic documentation. No third-party liability exposure identified.

case_facts.damage_description: charred kitchen cabinets above stove, smoke damage on ceiling and walls

rationale: Straightforward property damage claim: wind caused physical damage to the insured structure (roof shingles on back porch overhang). No third-party involvement, no theft, no vehicle involved. Covered under homeowners property_damage coverage.
claim_summary: Jordan Lee (POL-1006) filed a low-severity property damage claim for wind damage to roof shingles on the back porch overhang. Four shingles were blown off during a windstorm last weekend. No water intrusion reported. Estimated repair cost: $400. Policy has $2,500 deductible and $1,000,000 coverage limit. Claim is straightforward and ready for adjuster assignment.
